data.title: Choose the correct answer for each question.
data.description: Practise B1 comparison structures including as...as, less, much/far + comparative, and the same as.
learningPoints: Use much, far and a bit to modify comparatives.
Use less + adjective for a lower degree.
Use the same as and different from accurately.

sections.explain: Use AS + adjective + AS when two things are equal in a quality.

words.word: My car is as fast as yours.
My car is as faster as yours.
My car is so fast than yours.

sections.explain: Use NOT AS + adjective + AS to show that one thing has less of a quality.

words.word: This test isn't as difficult as the last one.
This test isn't so more difficult than the last one.
This test isn't as difficult than the last one.

sections.explain: MUCH can strengthen a comparative adjective.

words.word: This route is much shorter than the other one.
This route is very shorter than the other one.
This route is much shortest than the other one.

sections.explain: A BIT can make a comparative difference sound small.

words.word: The blue jacket is a bit cheaper.
The blue jacket is a bit cheapest.
The blue jacket is a bit more cheap.
The new system is far better than the old one.
The new system is far best than the old one.
The new system is very more better than the old one.

sections.explain: LESS + adjective expresses a lower degree.

words.word: This option is less expensive than the first one.
This option is lesser expensive than the first one.
This option is less more expensive than the first one.

sections.explain: Use THE SAME AS to say two things are equal in a particular respect.

words.word: My phone is the same model as yours.
My phone is the same model than yours.
My phone is same model as yours.

sections.explain: Use DIFFERENT FROM for contrast between two things.

words.word: Her idea is different from mine.
Her idea is different than mine in standard British English here.
Her idea is more different from mine.

sections.summary: Using a comparative with repeated change.
sections.explain: Use comparative + AND + comparative to describe continuing change.

words.word: The weather is getting colder and colder.
The weather is getting more cold and more cold.
The weather is getting coldest and coldest.

sections.explain: THE + comparative, THE + comparative expresses a relationship between two changing things.

words.word: The more you practise, the easier it becomes.
The more you practise, easier it becomes.
More you practise, the more easy it becomes.
